summary: UnifiedExpressionVisitor compiles any expression AST node into a backend-native expression: it derives the backend method from the function key via the registry, recursively visits operands, resolves operand metadata and applies capability gating and reusable lowering. TypeContext holds input-scoped dtype evidence and native lowering state. It is also used by relation compilation and conform.
key_classes: UnifiedExpressionVisitor — single visitor dispatching all node types via function-registry lookup
TypeContext — input-scoped operand dtype resolution and lowering cache
ResolvedOperand — operand descriptor with native dtype evidence
_CallOperandResolver — resolves call operands against protocol signatures
key_functions: UnifiedExpressionVisitor(expression_system, *, execution_context, diagnostic_trace=None, conform_node_id=None, input_data=None) — construct a visitor
visit(node) — compile a node to a backend expression
extension_points: Dispatch is driven by function registry entries, so new operations need no visitor change
diagnostic_trace and conform_node_id hooks used by relation conform compilation
lifecycle_notes: b7e9128b feat(371): reuse permitted expression lowerings within input scopes
b5074702 perf(capabilities): bypass expression gates without policy candidates
risks: visitor.py is ~1000 lines combining dispatch, option handling, capability gates and lowering reuse
Behaviour depends on execution_context being supplied (required keyword)
Input-scoped lowering cache invalidation is subtle
open_questions: Exact semantics of the reusable-lowering cache and TypeContext scoping were skimmed, not traced end to end.

evidence.detail: unified-visitor principle: one visitor, registry dispatch
